reference_solution: Use an OrderedDict from key to an entry containing value and absolute expires_at. `get` checks expiration, deletes stale state, and moves a live key to the most-recent end. `set` validates TTL, purges expired entries using one clock reading, overwrites and moves the key, then evicts from the least-recent end until within capacity. `len` purges expired entries before returning the count. The executable implementation is `reference.py`.
explanation: A dictionary gives key lookup while OrderedDict provides deterministic least-to-most-recent order. Injecting a monotonic clock makes expiration testable and immune to civil-time changes. A single `now` value per operation prevents inconsistent boundary decisions inside that operation. Purging before capacity eviction ensures expired entries never cause a live entry to be discarded.

alternatives.name: Hash map plus custom doubly linked list
alternatives.solution: Store nodes in a dict and splice nodes on access; maintain head and tail sentinels.
disadvantages: more invariants and implementation failure modes
no benefit for this standard-library exercise

alternatives.name: Expiration min-heap plus LRU order
alternatives.solution: Maintain a heap of expiration records alongside recency order and discard stale heap generations lazily.
advantages: avoids full scans when expiration is sparse
disadvantages: stale heap records require generations and memory controls

trade_off_analysis: Scanning the bounded cache during set and len is simple but O(capacity) in the worst case.
Lazy removal makes get O(1) but leaves unrelated expired entries until a purge operation.
A single instance lock can protect invariants, but get_or_load needs per-key coalescing and must not call external loaders while holding the global lock.

complexity.expected_time: get is O(1) average; set and len are O(capacity) worst case because they purge expired entries; final LRU eviction is O(1) per entry.
complexity.explanation: OrderedDict lookup, deletion, move_to_end, and popitem are constant average time; the explicit expiry scan dominates purge operations.

testing_and_debugging: Use a mutable fake clock; never sleep.
Test immediately before and exactly at expires_at.
Verify overwrite changes both value and TTL and moves recency.
Check internal order only while debugging; public tests should assert behavior.
production_follow_ups: Add hit, miss, expired, eviction, load latency, and current-weight metrics with bounded key cardinality.
Define thread/async ownership and per-key request coalescing.
Add weighted capacity, memory-pressure behavior, and safe shutdown only when requirements justify them.
critical_omissions: No concurrency or loader-stampede discussion in the production follow-up.
strong_response_example: I will use an OrderedDict and an injected monotonic clock. Expiration is `now >= expires_at`. Before evicting for capacity, I will remove expired entries so stale data cannot evict a live key. This makes get O(1) average and set O(capacity) worst case because of the simple purge; I would consider a generation-tagged heap only if measurements justify the extra complexity.

claims_constant_time: Ask which line removes unrelated expired entries
